question:
A 48-year-old woman with hypertension comes to the clinic reporting a 2-month history of walking
difficulties and left hip muscle weakness. During gait examination, she struggles to advance her right
foot when weight-bearing on her left foot. Left-sided standing flexion test is positive, and examination
reveals that both the right anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) and posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS)
are elevated. Bilateral Achilles and patellar reflexes are 2/4, with normal motor strength and sensation
in both lower extremities. Which somatic dysfunction best explains these findings? Answer Choices:
(A) Bilateral superior innominate shear (B) Left posteriorly rotated innominate (C) Right anteriorly
rotated innominate (D) Bilateral posteriorly rotated innominate (E) Left sacral torsion (F) Right superior
innominate shear (G) Left anteriorly rotated innominate (H) Left inferior innominate shear (I) Left
superior innominate shear (J) Right posteriorly rotated innominate
 A. Left posteriorly rotated innominate
B. Bilateral posteriorly rotated innominate
C. Bilateral superior innominate shear
D. Right superior innominate shear
E. Right anteriorly rotated innominate
F. Left sacral torsion
G. Right posteriorly rotated innominate
H. Left inferior innominate shear
I. Left superior innominate shear
J. Left anteriorly rotated innominate
